claims.statement: EU electricity rules define demand response as changing load for market signals or incentive payments and require participation through aggregation, supporting settlement for verified flexibility as the proposed paid event.

Transmission and distribution operators may procure ancillary services from aggregation participants, but the exact Polish payer, tariff, minimum bid, and margin for this small-site portfolio remain unverified.
The proposed control path is to sign meter-bound customer dispatch contracts and a replaceable market-access agreement; none is currently owned or contracted.
EU rules expressly contemplate independent aggregators and customer aggregation contracts, while leaving technical qualification and imbalance responsibility to applicable market arrangements.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Portfolio trading, balancing, or flexibility-procurement lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Remain vendor-neutral, give installers and asset owners transparent settlement splits, and support device mixes that single-vendor fleets ignore
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The installer or energy supplier until the asset owner signs a direct enrollment contract
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Opt-in referrals from solar, storage, heat-pump, and charger installers

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Installer revenue share and integration labor; hypothesis below 250 PLN per activated site
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Monthly or quarterly after market settlement; working capital is needed if customers are credited before partner remittance
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target of 45-65% after site incentives, market-access share, telemetry, and support
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Remote onboarding with occasional electrician intervention; target fewer than 45 minutes of human work per activated site per year
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Energy-market counsel, cyber controls, liability cover, audit logs, billing, and partner certification
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 10-20% of verified gross flexibility receipts, or a 20-50 PLN per-site monthly availability administration fee
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Telemetry/API charges, settlement share, customer incentive, metering exceptions, and device support

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Retailers, inverter vendors, and established aggregators can bundle enrollment into energy contracts or device apps
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is an accepted availability reservation or metered dispatch credited in a flexibility settlement; measurable loss is foregone settlement when a site cannot be qualified or verified
commercial_mechanics.payer: Licensed aggregator, balance-responsible party, retailer, or other flexibility buyer
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: The partner has more subscale devices than its existing onboarding and verification process can economically absorb
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Portfolio contract renews after demonstrated availability, dispatch success, and low exception cost

contrary_evidence: The right to aggregate does not prove that Polish small-site spreads cover telemetry, imbalance, support, and customer incentive costs.
Device makers and incumbent retailers may already control sufficient telemetry and distribution to bundle this function cheaply.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed 36-month customer aggregation contract for specified assets and event windows, paired with a separate settlement-integration agreement
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Route a consenting site through another licensed market-access partner, or exclude the unsupported device while retaining monitoring-only service
critical_control_point.current_owner: Each asset owner; no founder ownership or executed right is evidenced
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The installer or energy supplier until the asset owner signs a direct enrollment contract
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed 36 months; not negotiated or signed
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The parents' small renewable-installation firm could lawfully introduce a narrowly scoped pilot to consenting customers; it confers no current customer, dispatch, market, or data rights.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Asset owner together with a licensed aggregator or balance-responsible party
critical_control_point.renewal: Proposed annual renewal after the initial term, subject to performance and customer consent
critical_control_point.subject: Dispatch and telemetry rights for each enrolled battery, heat pump, or EV charger

economics.acquisition_route: One installer integration can expose many consenting sites; start with a lawful pilot through the family firm's ordinary commercial channel
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A large portfolio could compound recurring settlement share; reaching 5m PLN requires thousands of profitable sites or a strategic sale, with initial traction targeted in 12-18 months and scale evidence in 3-5 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day through a small pilot, automation-first monitoring, and outsourced electrical field work
economics.gross_margin_basis: Settlement share less customer incentive, market-access fee, telemetry, cloud, and exception support
economics.payback: Target under nine months on integration and site-onboarding cost; not yet evidenced
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 10-20% of verified settlement or 20-50 PLN per enrolled site per month
economics.retention_or_repeat: Recurring while assets remain enrolled and portfolio performance clears market thresholds

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A longitudinal response dataset by device, tariff, weather, and site improves qualification, bidding, and exception handling as the portfolio grows
fingerprint.customer: Licensed aggregators, balance-responsible parties, and energy retailers serving Polish small businesses
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable-energy installers embed a voluntary enrollment offer into commissioning and service visits
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Contract asset-level dispatch permissions, validate telemetry, route events, and split proceeds for a percentage of cleared flexibility revenue
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A market-access partner pays a platform share when enrolled capacity earns an availability or verified dispatch settlement
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A growing installed base of controllable behind-the-meter assets remains too fragmented to qualify, dispatch, verify, and settle one site at a time

founder_fit: Data-science skills map to baselines, response prediction, anomaly detection, and portfolio economics
A lawful installer relationship offers a small opt-in field test without claiming ownership of customers or data
Most operation can become event-driven software with exception-based support rather than constant networking
A pilot can be constrained to five hours per day and expanded only after positive per-site contribution
risks: Regulatory or contractual classification could require authorisation or a licensed principal
Failed dispatch can create imbalance charges, customer harm, or equipment warranty disputes
Installer referrals may not convert into durable direct customer contracts
A large aggregator could replicate the onboarding layer and compress the fee

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: percentage fee on verified flexibility settlement
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: time bounded customer grants to dispatch and settle named assets
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: qualification and market participation through a licensed aggregator or balance responsible party

structure.control_point: contracted dispatch windows and settlement instructions for enrolled assets
structure.critical_dependency: licensed market access plus accepted telemetry and baseline rules

thesis: Future operating state (2032): Polish small businesses automatically monetize controllable batteries, heat pumps, and EV chargers in flexibility markets. Missing contractual and coordination mechanism: meter-bound dispatch rights, telemetry validation, and settlement routing that a licensed aggregator or balance-responsible party can accept for many subscale sites.
title: Dispatch-Rights Rail for Small Energy Fleets
uncertainties: Polish market qualification, baseline, metering, and minimum portfolio requirements for each asset class
Actual controllable capacity and opt-in rate among small-business installer customers
Net settlement value after customer share, imbalance exposure, and market-access fees
Whether mixed-vendor APIs permit reliable dispatch without site hardware
